symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho>0\) is an analyst-specified radius of the abstract Gaussian decision experiment.

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w_j=P_n(X=j)\); in the Gaussian experiment, \(w\) is fixed at this observable-law coordinate.

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.def: \(\sigma_j^2=\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(Y\mid L=\ell,X=j)\), externally calibrated, known, and common over \(\ell\in\mathcal L\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.role: causal interpretation of the local target

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: \(q_{j,az}=P_n(A=a,Z=z\mid X=j)\) at the causal-null coordinate \(\delta_j=0\); in the Gaussian experiment, \(q\) is fixed at this observable null-law coordinate.

symbols.name: wCurve
symbols.role: declared weight in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: qCurve
symbols.role: declared cell law in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: sigmaCurve
symbols.role: declared externally calibrated scale in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: xiG
symbols.def: \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\), where \(w\) and \(q\) are fixed observable-law coordinates, \(\sigma\) is externally calibrated and known, and \(\rho\) is fixed by the abstract local decision design
symbols.role: complete index for every Gaussian decision object

symbols.name: Ecal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E(q)=\{\eta: q_{j,rs}=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\pi_j^{\ell}(1-\pi_j)^{1-\ell}a_{\ell j}^{r}(1-a_{\ell j})^{1-r}b_{\ell j}^{s}(1-b_{\ell j})^{1-s}\text{ for every }(j,r,s)\in\mathcal J\times\{0,1\}^2,\ \eta\text{ obeys the declared compact positivity, ordering, and proxy-relevance restrictions}\}\).

symbols.name: XiG
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak X_G=\{\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho):w_j\ge\epsilon\text{ for every }j,\ q_{j,az}>0\text{ for every }(j,a,z),\ \mathcal E(q)\ne\varnothing,\ \sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_j\le\sigma_{\max}\text{ for every }j\in\mathcal J,\ \rho>0\}\).
symbols.role: legal input set for the Gaussian frontier

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Order the four cells as \(c_1=00,c_2=01,c_3=10,c_4=11\). For positive \(q_j\), apply Gram--Schmidt in \(L_2(q_j)\) to \(d_{jr}(c)=\mathbf1\{c=c_r\}/q_j(c_r)-\mathbf1\{c=c_4\}/q_j(c_4)\), \(r=1,2,3\), fixing each sign by a positive first nonzero coordinate, to obtain \(e_{j1},e_{j2},e_{j3}\). Define \((B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}f)_r=\sum_{c}q_j(c)e_{jr}(c)f(c)\); then \(\|B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}f\|_2^2=\sum_{c}q_j(c)f(c)^2\) for every \(q_j\)-mean-zero \(f\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: For \(c=(a,z)\), \(k_{\xi_G,\eta j}(c)=\pi_j a_{1j}^{a}(1-a_{1j})^{1-a}b_{1j}^{z}(1-b_{1j})^{1-z}/q_{j,az}-\pi_j\), viewed in \(L_2^0(q_j)\); its notation retains the full experiment index even though only \(q\) enters this contrast directly.

symbols.name: aEtaEmbed
symbols.def: \(\widetilde a_{\eta,j}=\iota_j a_{\eta,j}\), where \(\iota_j:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^{3J}\) inserts its argument into block \(j\) and fills the other blocks with zero.

symbols.name: hRIF
symbols.role: unknown in the null-fiber compatibility system

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_J)\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\) is an analyst-specified state coordinate of the abstract Gaussian experiment.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q_g(dl,du)\) is a Markov kernel on ordered endpoints

symbols.name: Dval
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}\) is the two-measure dual value at the full experiment index \(\xi_G\)

symbols.name: Qstar
symbols.def: For a kernel \(Q\), let \(\overline Q(dg,dl,du)=\varphi_{3J}(g)dg\,Q_g(dl,du)\). \(Q_{w,q,\sigma,\rho}^{\star}=Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}\) is the unique minimizer over the optimal honest-kernel set of \(\iint K_{\mathrm{sel}}(x,x')\,d\overline Q(x)d\overline Q(x')\); if that set is empty, set \(Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}=Q^{\mathrm{full}}\).

symbols.name: Cprof
symbols.def: \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(g)=\operatorname{clhull}\{s\in[-\rho,\rho]:D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\le c_{\xi_G}(s)\}\) when this set is nonempty, and \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(g)=\{0\}\) otherwise.

symbols.name: wFace
symbols.role: declared weight in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: qFace
symbols.role: declared cell law in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: sigmaFace
symbols.role: declared externally calibrated scale in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: Winc
symbols.def: \(\omega=((\eta_r,j_r,\lambda_r))_{r=1}^R\) is represented by rational or real-algebraic coordinates and satisfies \(\sum_r\lambda_r\widetilde a_{\eta_r,j_r}=0\) and \(\sum_r\lambda_rw_{j_r}\ne0\).
symbols.role: exact nonregularity witness supplied to the pointwise certificate

symbols.name: marginXi
symbols.def: \(\gamma_{\xi_G,\omega}=\min\bigl(\{1,|\sum_r\lambda_rw_{j_r}|\}\cup\{|f|:f\ne0\text{ is a sign predicate in the fixed-input CAD and witness validation}\}\bigr)\). Zero predicates are recorded as active cells.
symbols.role: pointwise separation for exact branch validation

symbols.name: quadM
symbols.role: total directed Gaussian quadrature error budget

symbols.name: CcellsM
symbols.def: \(\mathscr C_M(\xi_G)=(C_{M,1},\ldots,C_{M,N_M^\Theta})\) is the lexicographically ordered list of every nonempty cell obtained by sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition of \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), refined by rational dyadic cuts until every cell has diameter at most \(h_M^{\Theta}\).

symbols.name: SM
symbols.def: \(S_M(\xi_G)=\{s_{M,r}:1\le r\le N_M^\Theta\}\), where \(s_{M,r}\) is the deterministic lexicographically least CAD sample point returned for the nonempty cell \(C_{M,r}\).

symbols.name: NpointM
symbols.def: \(N_M(\xi_G,\omega)\) is the product of the numbers of nonempty state cells, observation boxes, and ordered endpoint boxes at level \(M\), all in lexicographic order.

symbols.name: LipXi
symbols.def: \(A_{\xi_G}=1+\max_C\sup_{\vartheta\in C}\{\lVert Dm^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\lVert D\psi^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\rVert_2\}\), with the maximum over the finitely many smooth CAD strata and one-sided derivatives on their faces.

symbols.name: ellM
symbols.def: \(\ell_M(\xi_G,\omega)\) is the lexicographically tie-broken optimum of the finite directed-enclosure dual linear program whose two nonnegative weight vectors are supported only on \(S_M(\xi_G)\), whose first vector sums to one, and whose second sums to at most \(M\); the zero second measure is feasible.

symbols.name: uMraw
symbols.def: \(u_M(\xi_G,\omega)\) is the lexicographically tie-broken minimum objective among level-\(M\) endpoint-grid kernels satisfying every directed lower-coverage and upper-risk validation inequality; \(u_M\le2\rho\) through \(Q^{\mathrm{full}}\).

symbols.name: nuDom
symbols.def: \(\nu_{\mathrm{dom}}\) is a fixed \(\sigma\)-finite measure on the observed-data space.

symbols.name: Tbridge
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{com}}}\) contains \(0\) and is bounded uniformly in \(n\).

symbols.name: Pbridge
symbols.def: \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{com}}=(P_{n,\tau}:\tau\in\mathcal T_n)_{n\ge1}\) is one fixed-\(J\) observed-data triangular array with null law \(P_{n,0}\), target \(\theta(P_{n,\tau})\), and normalization \(\sqrt n\).
symbols.role: single source experiment for both reductions

symbols.name: Qred
symbols.def: \(Q_{\perp}\) is the deterministic matrix obtained by projecting the lexicographically ordered standard basis onto \(\ell^{\perp}\), applying Gram--Schmidt, and discarding zero residuals; its \(2m-1\) columns are orthonormal and span \(\ell^{\perp}\)

symbols.name: vBridge
symbols.def: \(v\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mathrm{com}}}\) indexes the path \(r\mapsto P_{n,rv}\) at \(r=0\)

symbols.name: gMom
symbols.role: common full moment tangent before quotienting

symbols.name: scoreG
symbols.role: common score construction for both reductions

symbols.name: AGmap
symbols.def: For each column \(\dot{\widetilde M}_{n,r}\), lift only within the quotient by \(g_{n,r}=Q_{\perp}\dot{\widetilde M}_{n,r}\in\ell^{\perp}\), split it as \(g_{n,r}=(g^D_{n,r,c},g^{YD}_{n,r,c})_{c=1}^m\), and set \(\dot\mu_{n,r,c}=\{g^{YD}_{n,r,c}-E_{P_{n,0}}[Y\mid D_c=1]g^D_{n,r,c}\}/P_{n,0}(D_c=1)\). Define \(A_n^G\dot{\widetilde M}_n=(\sqrt{w_j}B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}(\dot\mu_{n,r,c})_{c:\,X=j}/\sigma_j)_{j,r}\), and represent every generating direction by the reduced score \(s_{g_{n,r}}\).

symbols.name: AZmap
symbols.def: \(A_n^Z\) is obtained by rewriting the observable functional and influence-function formula in Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 as functions of \(\widetilde M_n\), differentiating them along each column \(\widetilde g_{n,r}\) of \(\dot{\widetilde M}_n\), and representing that direction by \(s_{g_{n,r}}=\widetilde g_{n,r}^{\mathsf T}\widetilde V(P_{n,0})^{-1}Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}\{\phi-E_{P_{n,0}}\phi\}\), where \(g_{n,r}=Q_{\perp}\widetilde g_{n,r}\in\ell^{\perp}\). No inverse of the singular \(2m\)-dimensional covariance is used.
symbols.role: published-comparator score construction on the quotient

symbols.name: redNull
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_n^G\) is derived from \(A_n^G\dot{\widetilde M}_n\) and the reduced score representers \(s_{g_{n,r}}\) in \(\mathrm{lem:common\text{-}score\text{-}bridge}\).

symbols.name: redZhou
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_n^Z\) is derived from \(A_n^Z\dot{\widetilde M}_n\) and the same reduced score construction in \(\mathrm{lem:common\text{-}score\text{-}bridge}\).

symbols.name: sNull
symbols.def: \(s_n^G\) is the closed linear span in \(L_2^0(P_{n,0})\) of the functions \(s_{g_{n,r}}\) for the reduced moment directions selected by \(A_n^G\dot{\widetilde M}_n\)

symbols.name: sZhou
symbols.def: \(s_n^Z\) is the closed linear span in \(L_2^0(P_{n,0})\) of the functions \(s_{g_{n,r}}\) for the reduced moment directions selected by \(A_n^Z\dot{\widetilde M}_n\)

symbols.name: Iscore
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_n\) is the linear correspondence induced by the identity embedding of the reduced-score spans \(s_n^G\) and \(s_n^Z\) in \(L_2^0(P_{n,0})\).
symbols.role: object tested by the agreement question

symbols.name: Mbridge
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{com}}\) is the primitive law class in \(\mathrm{def:common\text{-}overlap\text{-}class}\).
symbols.role: same-array domain for the conditional Zhou question

novel.justification: A validation study can bound the sensitivity contrast uniformly over finitely many prespecified strata.
External validation can supply a uniform lower bound on negative-control proxy relevance.
A common validated measurement protocol can place externally calibrated stratum scales in a prespecified compact range.

standard.name: uniform quadratic-mean differentiability with LAN remainder

novel.justification: Positive within-cell outcome variation is directly plausible for bounded clinical or biomarker outcomes after a finite observed-cell stratification and rules out deterministic outcomes inside any populated cell.

The [RED-COV] reduced-feature nondegeneracy condition is satisfied when finitely many observed cells remain populated, each cell retains genuine outcome variation, and the resulting quotient covariance eigenvalues stay uniformly separated from zero and infinity under a stable measurement protocol.

definitions.name: legal causal-null mechanism fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E(q)=\{\eta: q_{j,rs}=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\pi_j^{\ell}(1-\pi_j)^{1-\ell}a_{\ell j}^{r}(1-a_{\ell j})^{1-r}b_{\ell j}^{s}(1-b_{\ell j})^{1-s}\text{ for every }(j,r,s)\in\mathcal J\times\{0,1\}^2,\ \eta\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}overlap},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}ordering},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}separation}\}\).

definitions.name: product-Gaussian contrast-fiber experiment
definitions.construction: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), set \(\Theta_{\xi_G}=\{\vartheta=(\eta,t):\eta\in\mathcal E(q),\ t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\}\), with target \(\psi^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\), mean \(m^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\), and observation \(G_{\xi_G}\mid\vartheta\sim N_{3J}(m^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta),I_{3J})\).

definitions.name: randomized connected-interval rules
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_{\rho}=\{Q: g\mapsto Q_g\text{ is a Borel Markov kernel on }\mathcal A_{\rho}\}\).

definitions.name: honest connected-interval primal
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=V_{\xi_G}=\inf_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{\rho},v\in\mathbb R}v\) subject to \(r_{\xi_G,\vartheta}(Q)\le v\) and \(a_{\xi_G,\vartheta}(Q)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(\vartheta\in\Theta_{\xi_G}\).

definitions.name: two-measure endpoint dual
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}=\sup_{\Lambda,\Gamma}\{(1-\alpha)\Gamma(\Theta_{\xi_G})+\int_{\mathbb R^{3J}}\min_{(l,u)\in\mathcal A_{\rho}}\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda,\Gamma}(g;l,u)\,dg\}\), where \(\Lambda\) is a probability measure and \(\Gamma\) is a finite nonnegative measure on \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\).

definitions.name: determinate pointwise CAD primal--dual hierarchy
definitions.construction: Fix one rational or represented real-algebraic \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), one exact finite incompatibility witness \(\omega\), and \(M\ge1\). Use \(e_M=2^{-M-12}/(1+M)\), \(R_M=2^{-M}\lceil2^M\{K_{\xi_G}+\sqrt{3J/e_M}\}\rceil\), \(h_M^G=2^{-M}\), \(h_M^A=d_M=\min\{1,\rho\}2^{-M}\), \(h_M^{\Theta}=2^{-M}d_Me_M\min\{1,\gamma_{\xi_G,\omega}\}\), \(\zeta_M=e_M\), and \(\mathcal W_M=\{0,1\}\cup\{2^{-k}:1\le k\le M\}\). Exact sign-invariant CAD of the fixed set \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), followed by the stated dyadic refinement, produces the ordered nonempty cells \(\mathscr C_M(\xi_G)\) and the explicitly enumerated support \(S_M(\xi_G)\) containing exactly the deterministic lexicographic CAD sample point from each cell. Subdivide \([-R_M,R_M]^{3J}\) and \(\mathcal A_\rho\) by the declared rational meshes. Directed Gaussian quadrature is finite data: each observation--state--action box receives outward error at most \(\zeta_M/N_M(\xi_G,\omega)\), and the exact tail correction uses probability at most \(e_M\). A primal candidate is an endpoint-grid kernel constant on observation boxes, returns \([-\rho,\rho]\) outside the tail cube, dithers endpoints outward by \(\operatorname{Unif}[0,d_M]\), and mixes with \(Q^{\mathrm{full}}\) at a weight in \(\mathcal W_M\). It validates exactly when \(\underline a_{M,C}(Q)\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\overline r_{M,C}(Q)\le v\) for every \(C\in\mathscr C_M(\xi_G)\), where the directed enclosures optimize the mean, target, endpoints, and dither over the whole cell and add \(\Omega_{\xi_G,M}(h_M^{\Theta})\). Let \(u_M\) be the lexicographically tie-broken least validated \(v\). The dual optimizes only two finite nonnegative weight vectors on \(S_M(\xi_G)\); the first sums to one, the second sums to at most \(M\), so each measure has support at most \(|S_M(\xi_G)|\). Endpoint-box lower enclosures, per-box quadrature error \(\zeta_M\{1+\Gamma_M(\Theta_{\xi_G})\}/N_M\), and tail correction \(-e_M\Gamma_M(\Theta_{\xi_G})\) define its finite objective \(\ell_M\). Finally \(L_M=\max_{m\le M}\ell_m\), \(U_M=\min_{m\le M}u_m\), and the algorithm returns the first \(M\) with \(U_M-L_M\le\operatorname{tol}\).

definitions.name: coverage-calibrated profile-distance hull
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), compute \(D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\) and \(c_{\xi_G}(s)\). Return the closed hull of \(\{s\in[-\rho,\rho]:D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\le c_{\xi_G}(s)\}\) when nonempty, and return the fixed singleton \(\{0\}\) when empty; this convention is applied before any endpoint extraction.

definitions.name: primitive same-array score-map handle
definitions.construction: Start from the reduced feature \(\psi=Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}\phi\), its QMD identity \(\dot{\widetilde M}_n=Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}E_{P_{n,0}}[(\phi-E_{P_{n,0}}\phi)s_n^{\mathsf T}]\), and the common representer \(s_g=\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}\widetilde V(P_{n,0})^{-1}Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}(\phi-E_{P_{n,0}}\phi)\). Derive both \(A_n^G\dot{\widetilde M}_n\) and \(A_n^Z\dot{\widetilde M}_n\) from that one reduced moment derivative. Test whether the identity embedding of the resulting score spans preserves and reflects the affine influence-compatibility equations. Conditional on that bridge, compare endpoints only along the same \(P_{n,\tau_n}\), subsequence, normalization, and local labels.

statements.statement: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(k_{\xi_G,\eta j}\in L_2^0(q_j)\), the basis map \(B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}\) is an isometry on \(L_2^0(q_j)\), and \(m^G_{\xi_G}(\eta,t)\) is a continuous semialgebraic-chartwise analytic map on the compact state set \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\). Hence \(G_{\xi_G}\mid(\eta,t)\sim N_{3J}(m^G_{\xi_G}(\eta,t),I_{3J})\) is a well-defined dominated Gaussian experiment with target \(\psi^G_{\xi_G}(\eta,t)=\sum_jw_jt_j\).
statements.justification: This verifies the abstract Gaussian field and the regularity needed by the decision and certificate arguments.
statements.gap: Zwiernik--Smith characterize latent-tree fibers, but do not construct this posterior-contrast Gaussian field.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies the compact continuous state experiment used by the saddle and finite certificates.

statements.statement: Fix \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), let \(a_{\eta,j}=B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G,\eta j}\), and let \(\widetilde a_{\eta,j}=\iota_ja_{\eta,j}\in\mathbb R^{3J}\). A common regular linear influence coordinate for the Gaussian tangent system exists exactly when one \(h\in\mathbb R^{3J}\) satisfies \(\langle h,\widetilde a_{\eta,j}\rangle=w_j\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal E(q)\) and \(j\in\mathcal J\). The system is inconsistent exactly when finitely many legal pairs \((\eta_r,j_r)\) and coefficients \(\lambda_r\) satisfy \(\sum_r\lambda_r\widetilde a_{\eta_r,j_r}=0\) and \(\sum_r\lambda_rw_{j_r}\ne0\).
statements.justification: The exact affine compatibility system and its finite dual certificate make null nonregularity a checkable property rather than a geometric heuristic.
statements.gap: Kaji's Theorem 2 gives the generic impossibility result for weakly regular targets, while Theorems 5--6 establish the minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results; the proposed proposition supplies a hidden-treatment fiber criterion in observable moment coordinates.
statements.consumer: The criterion identifies exactly when centered Gaussian linear inference fails across the null fiber.

statements.statement: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), the honest connected-interval primal attains \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=V_{\xi_G}\), the two-measure dual attains the same value \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}=V_{\xi_G}\), and the characteristic-kernel selector does not take its fallback value and yields an attaining kernel \(Q_{w,q,\sigma,\rho}^{\star}=Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}\) supported for almost every \(g\) on minimizers of \((l,u)\mapsto\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star}}(g;l,u)\). Moreover, \(\Lambda^{\star}\) is supported on worst-length states in \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), \(\Gamma^{\star}\) is supported on binding-coverage states in \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), and these support and pointwise-minimization conditions are sufficient for optimality.
statements.justification: The saddle is the theorem-level decision frontier and produces both an optimal rule and an auditable least-favorable certificate.
statements.gap: Evans--Hansen--Stark optimize unrestricted randomized acceptance functions; connected realized intervals on a curved nuisance fiber require endpoint-kernel compactness and a different dual.
statements.consumer: The theorem is the sharp decision benchmark for every legal abstract Gaussian index.

statements.statement: Fix \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\) with rational or represented real-algebraic coordinates and mechanism bounds, and fix an exactly represented finite incompatibility witness \(\omega\). Every level \(M\) terminates by exact CAD, algebraic sign determination, finite directed Gaussian quadrature, and finite linear optimization. The dual weights are supported only on the enumerated set \(S_M(\xi_G)\), with each dual measure using at most \(|S_M(\xi_G)|\) atoms. The validation inequalities imply \(0\le L_M\le V_{\xi_G}\le U_M\le2\rho\). The CAD mesh is dense in every stratum, and the explicit bound \(\Omega_{\xi_G,M}(h_M^{\Theta})+(2\rho+1)A_{\xi_G}(h_M^G+h_M^A)+6e_M+2\zeta_M\to0\) controls state replacement, observation and action discretization, dithering, tails, and quadrature. Therefore \(L_M\uparrow V_{\xi_G}\) and \(U_M\downarrow V_{\xi_G}\). For every exact rational \(\operatorname{tol}>0\), the first \(M\) with \(U_M-L_M\le\operatorname{tol}\) is found after finitely many levels. No finite cover or uniform stopping level over \(\mathfrak X_G\) is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem makes every finite certificate level determinate and proves convergence through an explicit modulus and enumerated support.
statements.gap: Schafer--Stark give Monte Carlo convergence for finite prior polytopes and Schlemper--Moreira certify structured test inversion, but neither gives fixed-input matching endpoint-kernel certificates with exact branch decisions.
statements.consumer: The curved and active-face Gaussian benchmarks can be evaluated to any exact rational tolerance with an auditable primal--dual gap.

statements.statement: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), the rule \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}\) is Borel measurable and satisfies \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta_{\xi_G}}P_{\xi_G,\vartheta}\{\psi^G_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\in C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(G_{\xi_G})\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its semantic real-index regret is exactly \(R_{w,q,\sigma}^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)=R_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}\), and this regret is zero if and only if there exists an optimal dual pair \((\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star})\) for which the profile endpoint pair minimizes \(\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star}}(g;\cdot)\) almost everywhere and satisfies both complementary-slackness support conditions. No finite numerical evaluation of \(R_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}\) is asserted here; such an evaluation requires separate validated enclosures for the profile risk and the exact decidable input scope used for certified computation.
statements.justification: The theorem distinguishes valid profiling from decision-optimal profiling and makes zero regret certifiable.
statements.gap: Profile inversion is standard under weak identification, but no adjacent result gives an expected-length regret identity under a connected-hull action constraint.
statements.consumer: The saddle criterion separates honest profiling from decision-optimal profiling at a fixed Gaussian index.

statements.statement: Let \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}=((1),(41/100,9/100,9/100,41/100),(1),\rho)\), with \(J=1\), \(\epsilon=1/10\), and \(\rho>0\). Then \(\mathcal E(q^{\mathrm{face}})=\{\eta_0\}\), because \(\operatorname{Cov}_{q^{\mathrm{face}}}(A,Z)=4/25=\pi(1-\pi)(a_1-a_0)(b_1-b_0)\) attains the maximum allowed by the mechanism floor and ordering only at \(\eta_0=(1/2,1/10,9/10,1/10,9/10)\). At this element, \(k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},\eta_0}(00,01,10,11)=(-20/41,0,0,20/41)\), \(\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0)=B_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},1}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},\eta_0}\in\mathbb R^3\), and \(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}^2=w_1\|\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0)\|_2^2/\sigma_1^2=8/41\). Thus \(X_{G,\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}=\langle\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0),G_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\rangle/\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\sim N(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}t,1)\) for \(|t|\le\rho\). For \(0<\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\rho\le2z_{1-\alpha}\), \(V_{(1),q^{\mathrm{face}},(1)}(\rho)\) is the Evans--Hansen--Stark truncated-Pratt value divided by \(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\), and \(R_{(1),q^{\mathrm{face}},(1)}^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)>0\). The reproducible strictness certificate uses \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=-2\kappa(s+\rho)x+\kappa^2(s^2-\rho^2)\) for \(x<-\kappa\rho\), \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=(x-\kappa s)^2\) for \(|x|\le\kappa\rho\), and \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=2\kappa(\rho-s)x+\kappa^2(s^2-\rho^2)\) for \(x>\kappa\rho\), where \(\kappa=\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\): the calibrated acceptance endpoints fail the unique truncated-Pratt Neyman--Pearson endpoint condition on a positive-Lebesgue-measure set. At \(\alpha=0.05\) and \(\rho=1\), the legal inequality is \(\sqrt{8/41}<2z_{0.95}\).
statements.justification: The active face gives a fully legal strict-regret regime and a nontrivial reduction check against the known bounded-normal optimum.
statements.gap: Evans--Hansen--Stark solve the bounded-normal experiment but do not derive it from a hidden-treatment mechanism or compare the calibrated profile-distance hull.
statements.consumer: The proposition is a falsifiable benchmark for software and proves that profile inversion can be strictly longer even when it is honest.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{com}}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{com}}\), positive observed-cell probabilities and positive \(\operatorname{Var}_{P_{n,0}}(Y\mid D_c=1)\) imply \(\operatorname{Null}\{\operatorname{Var}_{P_{n,0}}(\phi)\}=\operatorname{span}\{\ell\}\). Every directional moment derivative \(g_{n,v}\) satisfies \(\ell^{\mathsf T}g_{n,v}=0\), is represented uniquely by \(\widetilde g_{n,v}=Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}g_{n,v}\), and has reduced-feature score \(s_{g_{n,v}}(O)=\widetilde g_{n,v}^{\mathsf T}\widetilde V(P_{n,0})^{-1}Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}\{\phi(O)-E_{P_{n,0}}\phi(O)\}\). Uniform QMD and the reduced identity \(\dot{\widetilde M}_n=Q_{\perp}^{\mathsf T}E_{P_{n,0}}[(\phi-E_{P_{n,0}}\phi)s_n^{\mathsf T}]\) then yield two reductions of the same central sequence: the null-fiber reduction \(\mathcal R_n^G\) and the Zhou reduction \(\mathcal R_n^Z\) are both constructed from these reduced scores. Both use the identical laws \(P_{n,\tau}\), local labels \(\tau\), target \(\theta(P_{n,\tau})\), and normalization \(\sqrt n\). This lemma does not assert that the two reduced-score spans are isomorphic or that their interval endpoints agree.
statements.justification: The reductions must be derived on the unique nonsingular quotient of one observed-data feature vector before any agreement question is meaningful.
statements.gap: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen provide their regular score representation, while no published result derives it jointly with the null-fiber score map from one reduced observable moment derivative.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies a noncircular domain on which the conditional score-bridge question can be asked.

statements.statement: On the primitive class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{com}}\), can one prove that the identity-induced correspondence \(\mathcal I_n\) between the reduced-score spans preserves and reflects the affine influence-function compatibility system of the two reductions? Conditional on that bridge, if \(\sqrt n\min_j\{w_j,\pi_j,1-\pi_j,a_{1j}-a_{0j},|b_{1j}-b_{0j}|,|\delta_j|\}\to\infty\), do the transported null-fiber interval and Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 centered interval have the same limiting endpoint law, coverage, and scaled expected length along every identical subsequence and identical local-alternative sequence? When an identification-relevant inverse or label-separation margin stays bounded, which common-array directions generate a nondegenerate fiber discrepancy? Distances of \(\sigma_j\) from \(\sigma_{\min}\) or \(\sigma_{\max}\) are not part of the agreement condition.
statements.justification: This isolates score compatibility and identification margins without defining the overlap class by the desired conclusion.
statements.gap: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 gives centered inference off the null but does not compare endpoint laws to a null-fiber interval on the same local array.
statements.consumer: A solution would delimit the exact regular subregion of the abstract null-fiber decision problem.

statements.statement: Let \(J=1\), \(\epsilon=1/10\), and \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}}=((1),(31/100,19/100,19/100,31/100),(1),\rho)\) for any \(\rho>0\). The three mechanisms \(\eta^{\mathrm{curv},1}=(1/2,1/5,4/5,3/10,7/10)\), \(\eta^{\mathrm{curv},2}=(1/2,3/10,7/10,1/5,4/5)\), and \(\eta^{\mathrm{curv},3}=(1/2,1/10,9/10,7/20,13/20)\) belong to \(\mathcal E(q^{\mathrm{curv}})\). Their posterior contrasts in \((00,01,10,11)\) order are \(k_1=(-25/62,-5/38,5/38,25/62)\), \(k_2=(-25/62,5/38,-5/38,25/62)\), and \(k_3=(-55/124,-25/76,25/76,55/124)\). They obey the exact relation \(-(9/5)k_1+(7/10)k_2+k_3=0\). Hence \(-(9/5)a_{\eta^{\mathrm{curv},1},1}+(7/10)a_{\eta^{\mathrm{curv},2},1}+a_{\eta^{\mathrm{curv},3},1}=0\), whereas \(-(9/5)w_1+(7/10)w_1+w_1=-1/10\ne0\). This is a finite dual witness for the inconsistency criterion in \(\mathrm{prop:null\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonregularity}\), so \(\theta\) has no common regular influence function at this worked null fiber.
statements.justification: The worked construction supplies an exact finite nonregularity certificate on a fully declared non-singleton fiber.
statements.gap: The latent-tree geometry literature describes fibers abstractly but does not give this hidden-treatment posterior-contrast instance as an indexed Gaussian decision benchmark.
statements.consumer: The instance is the prespecified exact input for certification at \(\rho\in\{1,2,4\}\) and an auditable nonregularity benchmark.

sampling_model.design: An abstract fixed-\(J\) product-Gaussian decision experiment indexed by \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\). The radius \(\rho\) is analyst specified; no sampled-data calibration or fallback rule is part of the proposal.
sampling_model.units: The Gaussian observation is \(G_{\xi_G}\in\mathbb R^{3J}\), with latent-mechanism state \(\eta\in\mathcal E(q)\) and bounded target coordinate \(t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal interpretation is the hidden binary exposure \(L\), with local target \(\psi^G_{\xi_G}(\eta,t)=\sum_jw_jt_j\).
sampling_model.overlap: The legal fiber enforces finite-stratum mass, latent prevalence, binary-mechanism compactness, surrogate ordering, and proxy separation; \(\sigma\) is a known Gaussian scale coordinate.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator or sampled-data transport is claimed. The only additional asymptotic object is the primitive bounded-outcome common array used to formulate the conditional Zhou score-map question after quotienting the exhaustive-indicator direction and imposing [RED-COV] nondegeneracy on the reduced feature covariance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and the stated nuisance-rate conditions, the observed-data influence-function estimator in Theorem 7 is asymptotically linear and yields centered Gaussian inference; its proof is in Supplement S17.
If \(\tau\le2z_{1-\alpha}\), the truncated Pratt procedure attains the minimax expected measure.
The smooth observed-law fiber is diffeomorphic to a disjoint union of polyhedra and is a manifold with corners.
The Monte Carlo confidence-set estimator converges to the \(\Gamma\)-minimax procedure for a polytope of priors.
Proposition 1 on page 24 shows that uniform approximation error \(\varepsilon\) changes coverage probability by at most \(\varepsilon\).
Estimator distributions and uniform test size are established over weak, semi-strong, and strong drifting sequences.
Weak-identification limit theory is combined with parameter-on-the-boundary theory in minimum-distance models.
At boundaries and singularities, likelihood-ratio asymptotics are determined by a non-linear tangent cone.
Theorem 2 gives the generic impossibility result for weakly regular targets, and Theorems 5--6 establish the minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results.

tldr: The proposal solves the honest connected-interval decision problem in the abstract hidden-treatment Gaussian null-fiber experiment and makes the solution computable through a determinate pointwise certificate hierarchy. At every exact rational or represented real-algebraic input, level \(M\) uses declared tail, observation, action, state, dither, safety, and quadrature schedules; an exact CAD enumerates one lexicographic sample point from every nonempty state cell, and the dual may place weight only on that finite set. Directed validation yields monotone \(L_M\uparrow V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\) and \(U_M\downarrow V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\), with convergence controlled by an explicit modulus and finite termination at rational tolerance. The exact affine nonregularity criterion has a finite worked witness, while the active face gives a legal strict-positive profile-regret regime. Zhou agreement remains a conditional same-array question built on the \(2m-1\)-dimensional reduced observable feature, its nonsingular covariance, and only identification-relevant inverse and label-separation margins.

project_justification.gap: Evans--Hansen--Stark solve special restricted-normal problems, Schafer--Stark analyze Monte Carlo approximation over finite prior polytopes, and Schlemper--Moreira bound coverage distortion from approximation. None gives a determinate two-sided continuum certificate for connected endpoint kernels over a curved latent fiber.
project_justification.niche: The decision program combines continuum coverage constraints, unbounded Gaussian observations, connected realized actions, and topology-changing semialgebraic nuisance fibers.
project_justification.fill: At each fixed decidable algebraic input, exact CAD supplies the enumerated support \(S_M\); finite directed quadrature and explicit validation inequalities produce monotone primal and dual bounds with a certified stopping rule.

related_work: Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 2) provide Bayes--minimax duality and the bounded-normal truncated-Pratt solution, but not a deterministic continuum certificate hierarchy for connected endpoint kernels on a curved Gaussian surface. Schafer and Stark (2009) establish Monte Carlo convergence over a finite polytope of priors, not matching deterministic bounds for the continuum problem. Schlemper and Moreira (2026, Proposition 1, page 24) relate uniform approximation error to coverage error, but do not optimize worst expected length. Zwiernik and Smith (2011, 2012, Theorems 5.4 and 5.8) supply the inequalities and cornered fiber geometry retained by the CAD subdivision. Kaji (2021, Theorems 2 and 5--6) informs the exact affine compatibility criterion. Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2024, Theorem 7 and Supplement S17) provide the off-null centered-inference comparator; the proposal treats their theorem as informing a conditional same-array score-map question, not as a result extended by the Gaussian saddle.
technical_internal_limitation: The certificate theorem is pointwise. Exact termination requires rational or represented real-algebraic inputs and an exact finite witness; an approximation oracle does not decide equality, rank, or active boundaries. The convergence proof must establish density of the lexicographic CAD samples in every stratum and verify the displayed continuity modulus together with the directed Gaussian enclosures. No finite cover or uniform stopping level is claimed over the unbounded legal index set. No sampled-data procedure, fallback interval, empirical calibration of \(\rho\), or application claim is included. The Zhou comparison remains conditional on proving that the two reduced-score spans preserve and reflect the same affine compatibility system.
honest_scope: The connected saddle, profile-regret identity, active-face strictness result, and finite certificate concern only the abstract Gaussian experiment. The hierarchy is pointwise in one exact decidable input, one exact incompatibility witness, and one rational tolerance. The radius \(\rho\) is an analyst-specified coordinate. There is no sampled-data lift or consumer reanalysis claim. The Zhou question is posed on a primitive dominated fixed-\(J\) bounded-outcome array with uniform QMD, positive observed cells, positive within-cell outcome variance, and [RED-COV] nondegeneracy of \(\widetilde V(P_{n,0})\) on \(\ell^{\perp}\); the two reductions are lemma conclusions from the same reduced moment derivative. Endpoint agreement is asked only conditionally on a reduced score-space bridge and divergence of identification-relevant inverse and label-separation margins, with no variance-boundary margins and no converse.

literature_map: Evans--Hansen--Stark provide abstract decision duality and a bounded-normal solution; Schafer--Stark provide Monte Carlo approximation over finite prior polytopes; Schlemper--Moreira relate numerical approximation to coverage; and Zwiernik--Smith characterize legal inequalities and cornered latent-tree fibers. These results leave open a deterministic pointwise hierarchy with enumerated CAD support, directed Gaussian enclosures, continuum validation, and matching connected-endpoint bounds. Kaji motivates the exact affine compatibility criterion. Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen is used only as an informed-by comparator for the primitive same-array score-map question.
